correctness.rationale: Every one of the 24 monic integer trinomials has its exact factor multiplication checked in the enclosed 24-row certificate. All 28 distinct nonlinear factors have squarefree modular witnesses for irreducibility and required Frobenius permutation types, with discriminant checks. Irreducible prime-degree seven plus transposition forces S7; six-degree primitivity from a 5-cycle plus transposition forces S6; the quartic 4- and 3-cycles force S4; irreducible cubics with discriminants -23/-31 have S3. For the two-factor cases, different unique quadratic subfields preclude all common nontrivial quotient fields and force S3xS3 or S3xS4. The included verifier was run successfully from the same package; the group-theoretic deductions are explicitly proved in RESULT.md. The result is exact for all 24 cases, not an extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 result explicitly assumes degree greater than eight for coefficient-product magnitude two, so does not determine degree-seven groups. The 2019 work classifies factorization of bounded norm; its factorization information does not establish the exact 24 splitting-field groups or that two nonlinear factors have disjoint splitting fields. Earlier trinomial Galois studies are primarily irreducible-case theorems. The matched statement includes the direct-product assertions; targeted literature and published-record searches did not disclose coverage. Substantial residual risk remains from implicit coverage or unpublished computations, not treated as novelty proof.
residual_risks: The entire 24-case table could be implicit in broader number-field databases, low-height polynomial catalogues or unpublished computations.
The searched record index is not exhaustive and ranked misses are possible; absence of hits is not a uniqueness proof.
The value lies mainly in the direct-product compositum classification; individual factor Galois groups are susceptible to coverage by earlier general sufficient conditions.

value.rationale: Degree seven is a natural low-degree exception to the coefficient-two threshold of the October 2026 theorem, and the input range exhausts all nonconstant middle exponents for a prime degree. The classification makes a qualitative distinction between individual irreducibility (eight S7), a rational root (eight S6), and two different reducible splitting-field architectures (S3xS3 or S3xS4). Distinct quadratic subfields establish that the nonlinear factor fields are independent, which is not a routine conclusion of factorization alone and supplies a useful exact boundary example for maximal-permitted-Galois heuristics. Only this finite motivated domain is claimed.
